learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts regarding the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving problems typical of engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling the learning of new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Critical thinking. To reason reflectively on a topic, being able to deliberate on its validity by subjecting one's own and external convictions to debate.
Knows the units and orders of magnitude of defined physical quantities and solves basic engineering problems, expressing the numerical result in appropriate physical units.
Correctly uses basic experimental measurement or simulation methods and processes, presents, and interprets the obtained data, relating them to appropriate physical quantities and laws.
Knows the concepts, main properties, and fundamental laws of electromagnetic fields and waves, and their application to basic engineering problems.
Knows and uses concepts related to capacitance, electric current, self-induction and mutual induction, as well as the basic electrical and magnetic properties of materials.

Knows the wave equation, the characteristic parameters of its basic solutions, and their energetic aspects. Analyzes the propagation of mechanical waves in fluids and solids and knows the fundamentals of acoustics.

Recognizes the properties of electromagnetic waves, basic propagation and superposition phenomena, the electromagnetic spectrum, basic aspects of light-matter interaction, and the applications of these phenomena in technology.
Analyzes problems integrating different aspects of Physics II, recognizing the varied physical foundations underlying technical applications, devices, or real systems.
Uses bibliography, by any currently available means, and uses clear and precise language in explanations about physics issues.

syllabus_topics: Topic 5: Waves in solids and fluids. Acoustics
assessment_rules: The course is evaluated through global assessment, but an intermediate test is scheduled to facilitate gradual progression. For continuous assessment, a written test on topics 1-4 accounts for 45% (if score is at least 4.5 out of 10), a written test on topics 5-7 accounts for 35%, and an exam on laboratory practices accounts for 20%. For global assessment, a comprehensive exam on topics 1-7 accounts for 80%, and an exam on laboratory practices accounts for 20%. Students who have not attended practical sessions will be additionally evaluated through a practical lab exam. The use of non-permitted materials during evaluation may result in withdrawal from the exam and a grade of 0.
